name: Happy path
description: All 4 nodes decide value A in round 0

name: Timeout and prevote nil
description: p1 times out on propose, prevotes nil, but still locks and decides A via late PROPOSAL

name: Cross-round decision
description: p3 times out through all phases, decides A from round 1 using round 0 evidence

name: Locking behavior
description: All nodes lock on A but timeout before deciding, move to round 1 with lockedValue=A

name: Round skip (L55)
description: p2,p3 skip to round 1 via L55 after seeing f+1 messages from round 1

name: Reached round 1
description: All nodes timeout in round 0 and move to round 1

name: User strike and proposal ack
description: p1 user-acks an engine-struck PROPOSAL; separately, a user-strike+unstrike pair cancels at the same anchor.

name: GST recovery after missed proposal
description: p1 hides and times out on a proposal before GST; GST reveals it and post-GST protocol actions lead all nodes to decide A

name: Byzantine proposal equivocation
description: p0 is Byzantine and proposes A to p1, p2 and B to p3. B gets only 2 prevotes, so no correct node can decide B. p1 and p2 decide A. After GST, gossip gives p3 the PROPOSAL(A) and the precommits, and p3 decides A.

name: Byzantine silent proposer and GST
description: p0 is Byzantine and sends nothing. p1, p2, p3 time out through round 0 and go to round 1. After GST, the round 1 proposer p1 proposes A and the correct nodes decide A without p0.

name: Byzantine vote equivocation and split lock
description: p3 is Byzantine. It prevotes A to p1 and nil to p0, p2, so only p1 locks A in round 0. In round 1, p1 proposes A with vr=0, but p0 and p2 have no polka for A. After GST, gossip gives them p3's PREVOTE(A), L28 is enabled, and the correct nodes decide A.

name: Byzantine amnesia
description: In round 0, p3 is correct and precommits A. p0 decides A. p3 then becomes Byzantine, ignores its lock, and prevotes B in round 1. p2 is locked on A and prevotes nil, so B has no polka. p1 and p2 decide A.
